'''Sir James Hough'''{{pronunciation needed|date=December 2023}} (born 6 August 1945)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Hough, Prof. James | id = U44099 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.44099 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is a British [[physicist]] and an international leader in the search for [[gravitational wave]]s.<ref>{{cite web | title=Newsletter of the Institute of Physics in Scotland | url=http://www.iop.org/activity/branches/Scotland/Newsletter/file_10638.pdf|access-date= 23 March 2007}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref><ref>[http://www.physics.gla.ac.uk/igr/index.php?content=bio&person=jhough Institute of Gravitational Research – Member Biography]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110724180621/http://dept.physics.gla.ac.uk/staff/default.asp?record=99 University of Glasgow Staff Profile]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110724180621/http://dept.physics.gla.ac.uk/staff/default.asp?record=99 List of publications]</ref><ref>[http://www.iop.org/activity/awards/Senior_Awards/The_Duddell_Medal_and_Prize/page_1786.html Duddell Medal and Prize]</ref>

==Career and research==
Hough has held the following professional positions:
* Professor of [[experimental physics]] at the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Institute of Gravitational Research – Member Biography | url=http://www.physics.gla.ac.uk/igr/index.php?content=bio&person=jhough|access-date= 2 May 2007}}</ref> 
* Director of the Institute of Gravitational Research at the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Institute of Gravitational Research – Member Biography | url=http://www.physics.gla.ac.uk/igr/index.php?content=bio&person=jhough|access-date= 2 May 2007}}</ref>
* Member of the [[LISA (astronomy)|LISA]] International Science Team.<ref>{{cite web | title=LISA Science Team Membership | url=http://www.srl.caltech.edu/lisa/people/list.html | access-date=2 May 2007 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070703191658/http://www.srl.caltech.edu/lisa/people/list.html | archive-date=3 July 2007 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>
* Delegate to the [[LIGO]] Council.<ref>{{cite web | title=LIGO Council| url=http://admdbsrv.ligo.caltech.edu/roster/lsc_roster.htf?rosterid=council}}</ref>
* Chair of the ''Education, Training and Careers Committee'' and the ''Fellowships Panel'' of the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Science & Technology Facitities Council – Committee Information| url=http://www.scitech.ac.uk/About/Strat/Archive/PPARC/E_and_T.aspx|access-date= 2 May 2007}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
* 2003 Hough was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/james-hough-11650/|title=James Hough Biography|publisher= Royal Society|access-date= 19 November 2017}}</ref>
* 2004 Hough was awarded the [[Duddell Medal|Duddell Medal and Prize]], a senior award from the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Recipients of the Duddell award| url=http://www.iop.org/activity/awards/Senior_Awards/The_Duddell_Medal_and_Prize/Duddell_award_recipients/page_10137.html|access-date= 2 May 2007}}</ref> The award is made annually to "an individual or team for outstanding contributions to the advancement of knowledge through the application of physics, including invention or design of scientific instruments or by the discovery of materials used in their construction."<ref>{{cite web | title=The Duddell Medal and Prize| url=http://www.iop.org/activity/awards/Senior_Awards/The_Duddell_Medal_and_Prize/page_1786.html|access-date= 2 May 2007}}</ref>
* 2008 Hough was awarded the [[Gunning Victoria Jubilee Prize]] of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] for his work on gravitational waves<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.rse.org.uk/cms/files/research_awards/prizes/prize_lists/gunning_victoria_winners.pdf| title=Gunning Victoria Jubilee Prize Lectureship|publisher= RSE|access-date=19 November 2017}}</ref>
* 2013 Hough was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the 2013 Birthday Honours for services to science.<ref name=gaz31712>{{London Gazette|issue=60534|supp=y|page=11|date=15 June 2013}}</ref>
* 2015 Hough was awarded the Institute of Physics [[Phillips Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Phillips Award recipients |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/phillips-award |website=www.iop.org |publisher=[[Institute of Physics]] |access-date=14 July 2021}}</ref>
* 2018 Awarded the [[Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society]] for Astronomy<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2020-01/Gold%20Medallists.docx.pdf|title=The Gold Medal|publisher=[[Royal Astronomical Society]] (RAS) |website=ras.ac.uk|access-date= 25 August 2020}}</ref>
* 2019 Hough was knighted (Knight Bachelor) by The Duke of Cambridge during a ceremony at Buckingham Palace on 31 January 2019, in recognition of Hough's international leadership in the search for gravitational waves ~ 'ripples' in the fabric of space-time.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.gla.ac.uk/news/headline_632985_en.html| title=Knighthood for Groundbreaking UofG Astrophysicist|publisher= UofG|access-date=3 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/notice/3369106|title=London Gazette, no 3369106|website=www.thegazette.co.uk|access-date=20 July 2021}}</ref>
* 2020 Hough was awarded the Royal Society's Bakerian Medal in 2020<ref>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/bakerian-lecture/ |title=Bakerian Medal and Lecture |website=royalsociety.org |publisher=[[Royal Society]]|access-date=14 July 2021}}</ref>
*2021 Became Honorary Liveryman of the [[Worshipful Company of Scientific Instrument Makers]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2021}}

===Appearances in media===
Hough received widespread media coverage in 2004 when he placed a [[Gambling|bet]], against the [[odds]], of detecting gravitational waves before 2010. The original odds were set at [[Odds|500/1]], but following huge interest, the [[Sports betting|betting]] company were forced to cut their odds to [[Odds|6/1]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bookmakers slash odds on science | url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/3613510.stm |work=BBC News |access-date= 2 May 2007 | date=31 August 2004}}</ref>

In April 2007, during the run-up to the [[Scottish Parliament]]ary elections, Hough signed an [[open letter]], along with sixty-one other top Scottish scientists, backing the retention of the [[Acts of Union 1707|Union]] between [[Scotland]] and England.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Times – Letters to the Editor |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/comment/debate/letters/article1706486.ece |access-date=5 May 2007 |location=London }}{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=The Scotsman – Politics| url=http://thescotsman.scotsman.com/politics.cfm?id=655262007| archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715155640/http://thescotsman.scotsman.com/politics.cfm?id=655262007| url-status=dead| archive-date=15 July 2012| access-date=5 May 2007}}</ref> They were concerned that [[Scottish independence]] would have "detrimental consequences for the health of the Scottish science base and for the long term viability of the Scottish economy and society."
